newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Getronics profits jump, eyes buys.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Getronics profits jump, eyes buys.

text.p: Getronics NV, one of a new breed of Dutch high-tech firms, announced 35 percent higher 1996 net profits on Friday and said it expected continued growth.
Net profit came in at 131.6 million guilders ($69.2 million) versus a previous 97.5 million guilders. Earnings per share rose 33.3 percent to 1.52 guilders per share.
"We think 20 percent growth in earnings per share should be possible in the coming years," chairman Ton Riseeuw told a news conference.
Getronics' turnover has doubled in the last five years to more than 2.2 billion guilders last year, and the group said it was actively seeking acquisitions in its existing markets.

The group, which offers information and telecoms technology and information systems management, generates some 30 percent of its turnover outside The Netherlands -- in Spain, Norway and Belgium -- but these activities contribute less than 30 percent of profits.
Risseeuw said Getronics' position in Spain, for example, was too small, with just 200 staff in a nation of 50-60 million people.

But he said the group's primary focus was in The Netherlands where it was interested in buying state-owned payroll processor Roccade, but he added he was lining up alternatives if a bid was unsuccessful.
"We want to expand internationally, but a solid home base is necessary," he said.
Risseeuw said the Dutch government had put too high a price on Roccade, but declined to elaborate. Roccade's sell-off has been slated for July.
Dutch media said last year that The Hague had delayed Roccade's privatisation because other parties, including U.S. Electronic Data Systems, had offered more money.
Asked whether Getronics could buy Roccade and complete a major foreign acquisition, Risseeuw said the group could always issue new shares.
"That money would be forthcoming...we could always issue new shares," he said.

Getronics, which had 1996 turnover of 2.2 billion guilders, sees future sales being boosted by up to 500 million guilders due to systems changes forced by the millennium and the advent of the single European currency.

Risseeuw said the company eyed about five percent of the estimated 10 billion guilders extra turnover in the Dutch market coming from changes that systems and program operators would have to make by 1999 and 2000.
"We expect to get about five percent of this market which we have estimated at 10 billion guilders," he said.
Risseeuw said he expected "explosive" growth in demand from customers facing problems ahead of the introduction of the euro and the arrival of the millennium.
But he forecast a fall-off after 1998 by which time new systems would have to be in place to cope with the changes.
In a weaker Amsterdam market, Getronics shares shed 2.50 guilders to 62.50 each.
